High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore

sentences.text:
Appearance:
 Shri Akash Sharma - Advocate for the applicant.
Shri Hemant Sharma-GA appearing on behalf of Advocate   Shri Naman Raj Singh Rathore,Advocate for the responde

2] This petition has been filed by the petitioner under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for quashing the FIR lodged at Crime No.1350/2023 at Police Station - Banganga District Indore under Section 363 IPC and after arrest of the petitioner and medical of the prosecutrix Section 366, 376(2)(N), 344 IPC and 3/4 of POCSO Act and the subsequent proceedings arising out of the said crime number.
3] Counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the parties have settled their dispute out of the Court.

Since both the parties are also present in the Court, and on a query made by this Court, the complainant and the prosecutrix have also stated that they have already compromised the matter and the prosecutrix has also married the applicant, and out of the wedlock, she has a child and does not intend to prosecute the petition any further.
4] Counsel for the petitioner, at the outset, has submitted that the parties have settled their disputes amicably out of the Court.

It is also submitted that an application I.A.No.11692/2024 and I.A. No.11693/2024 under Section 320 of the Cr.P.C.,1973 along with an affidavit of the complainant has also NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35506 2 MCRC-30278-2024 been filed.
It is also submitted that no purpose would be served to keep the matter pending when the matter is already compromised, and in such circumstances, the petition may be allowed.

1 5] Counsel for the petitioner has also submitted that considering the fact that the matter has already been compromised between parties, no purpose would be served to further drag the trial, the result of which is a foregone conclusion.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, it is submitted that the petition be allowed, and the FIR and the subsequent proceedings be quashed.
In support of his submission, counsel for the petitioner has also relied upon a decision rendered by the Supreme Court in the case of Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab reported as (2012) 8 SCR 753.

entities.text: Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab reported as (2012) 8 SCR 753
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5] Counsel for the respondent No.1/State, has submitted that appropriate orders may be passed and has also submitted that the trial is at the stage of evidence but the prosecutrix has not been examined till date.

Having considered the rival submissions and on perusal of the case-diary as also the documents filed on record and further considering the fact that the matter has been compromised between the parties, this Court is of the considered opinion that no purpose would be served to further waste the valuable time of the trial court in this case, the result of which is a forgone conclusion, and thus, is inclined to allow the present petition as further proceedings against the petitioner before the Trial Court would only be an exercise in futility.

7] Resultantly, the petition is hereby allowed and the FIR bearing Crime No.1350/2023 at Police Station - Banganga District Indore under Section 363 IPC and after arrest of the petitioner and medical of the prosecutrix Section 366, 376(2)(N), 344 IPC and 3/4 of POCSO Act and other consequential proceedings arising out of the said crime number, so far as it relates to the present petitioner, are hereby quashed.
8] With the aforesaid, the petition stands allowed and disposed of.
(SUBODH ABHYANKAR) JUDGE NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35506 3 MCRC-30278-2024 das Rohit vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143247371/
